_comment: Worked example: register a LOCAL DEV Notion public connection (OAuth) and capture its client id/secret.
Built from a real hand-driven agent-browser session (comet profile, CDP 127.0.0.1:9222, --session comet).
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by pixel (not part of the Flow schema); they are documentation for humans.
pixel flow run notion-oauth-app --var accept_terms=true [--var app_name='My Local Dev App'] [--var callback_url=http://localhost:3000/oauth/notion/callback]
TERMS: accept_terms defaults to false. Creating a Notion connection implies accepting Notion's Developer Terms, so the
'Create connection' click is gated behind --var accept_terms=true. Without it the flow stops with the form filled and nothing created.
THE SECRET IS SHOWN ONCE in a dialog opened by 'Show client secret'. The flow ends with that dialog open; run the capture
command immediately and do not close the dialog first. pixel-flow cannot write files and `pixel flow run` discards `eval`
output, so oauth-env.py reads the dialog straight into $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600) and prints only lengths.
There is no credential sanity check for Notion in oauth-env.py (none was established in the recorded session).
LOGIN IS OUT OF SCOPE. The comet session must already be signed in to Notion. A login page makes the flow STOP on purpose
(a `click` whose ref_hint can never match). It never types credentials. Sign in by hand, then re-run.
NOT IDEMPOTENT: every run creates a NEW connection. Delete stale local-dev connections by hand in the console.
AFTER THE FLOW (manual follow-up): your backend/app reads OAUTH_NOTION_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_NOTION_CLIENT_SECRET from its
process environment. `source` the env file written to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT before starting the API. Never commit that file.
NEVER put real client ids or secrets in this file.
name: notion-oauth-app
title: Register a local-dev Notion OAuth connection and capture client id/secret
description: Creates a Notion OAuth connection (default name 'My Local Dev App', installable in any workspace, default capabilities) with the local callback as redirect URI, then reveals the one-time client secret and stops with the dialog open. Follow immediately with `oauth-env.py capture notion` to write OAUTH_NOTION_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_NOTION_CLIENT_SECRET to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600). Create is gated behind --var accept_terms=true (default false). Login is out of scope; the flow stops if signed out. Not idempotent.
preconditions: Verify comet-cdp is up (port 9222) and `agent-browser --session comet tab list` answers
The comet browser profile is ALREADY signed in to Notion (this flow never types credentials)
Read Notion's Developer Terms yourself; pass --var accept_terms=true only if you accept them (default false: the flow stops before creating anything)
Export OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> before the capture step (the file receives secrets: keep it out of git, mode 600 is enforced)

vars.name: homepage_url
vars.description: Accepted for a uniform interface with the other oauth-app flows; the recorded Notion creation form needed no homepage, so it is unused

vars.name: callback_url
vars.description: Redirect URI your local app's OAuth callback route listens on

vars.name: accept_terms
vars.description: 'true' lets the flow click 'Create connection', which implies accepting Notion's Developer Terms. Anything else (including omitted) stops the flow before creating. Must be passed with --var; it has no effective default

steps.rationale: Open the integrations page. It redirects to https://app.notion.com/developers/connections. Already-authenticated profile expected.
steps.on_failure: If the open times out, re-run `agent-browser --session comet tab list` and retry once

steps.rationale: PITFALL: the cross-domain redirect to app.notion.com takes a moment; do not snapshot the pre-redirect page
Login is out of scope. A signed-out profile lands on the Notion login page; stop instead of touching credentials.
steps.condition: page shows 'Continue with Google' or 'Continue with email' or 'Enter your email' or 'Log in to Notion'

then.rationale: STOP: not signed in to Notion in the comet session. Sign in by hand in Comet, then re-run this flow. (Fails on purpose: the ref_hint can never match, so the flow aborts with this message.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - Notion login required in the comet session - a human must sign in, then re-run the flow

steps.rationale: Capture the connections list; look for the 'New connection' button
Start a new connection
Let the creation form render
Capture the form: Connection name, type radios (OAuth / API token), Installable in, Redirect URIs, Create connection
Connection name
Choose the 'OAuth' connection type (NOT 'API token', which has no client id/secret). The two quoted terms make the matcher require a radio line that also says OAuth.
steps.on_failure: Re-snapshot; if the type picker is cards or tabs instead of radios, click the one labelled OAuth.

steps.rationale: Installable in: leave the default 'Any workspace'. The Redirect URIs field should now be visible.
PITFALL: Redirect URIs is a token/chip input. Type the callback URL (real key events), then press Enter in the next step to commit it as a chip.
PITFALL: Enter commits the URL as a chip. Until then a suggestions dropdown COVERS the Create connection button and the click would land on a suggestion instead.
Let the chip render and the dropdown close
Verify the redirect URI chip, the name and OAuth type before creating

TERMS GATE: creating a connection implies accepting Notion's Developer Terms. Click 'Create connection' ONLY when --var accept_terms=true was passed. Unset or any other value does NOT click (fail-closed: {{accept_terms}} is not defaulted, so an omitted var stays a literal and never equals 'true'). Passing accept_terms=true means the human accepts the terms.
Creation redirects to https://app.notion.com/developers/connections/<uuid>
Still on the form means Create did not fire: accept_terms was not true, or a required field is missing. Nothing was created. Stop.

then.rationale: STOP: the creation form is still open. Either accept_terms was not true (re-run with --var accept_terms=true after reading Notion's Developer Terms) or a required field is missing. Nothing was created. (Fails on purpose.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - Notion connection was not created - accept_terms must be true and name, OAuth type and redirect URI must be set

steps.rationale: Confirm the connection page. Its URL ends in the connection uuid, which IS the OAuth client id. Default capabilities (read, update, insert content) are enough; leave them.
Reveal the secret. PITFALL: it appears ONCE in a dialog; the capture command must run before the dialog is closed or the page reloads (the secret can only be regenerated, not re-read).
steps.on_failure: Never click twice or press Escape: closing the dialog loses the one-time view.

steps.rationale: Let the dialog render

FLOW ENDS HERE with the one-time secret dialog open (secret starts with secret_ or ntn_; client id = uuid in the URL). DO NOT CLOSE THE DIALOG. NEXT: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture notion

success_signal: page text contains 'client secret' (the one-time secret dialog is open). Then immediately run: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> oauth-env.py capture notion
